NKE.rationale: Nike is in a severe fundamental deterioration with no credible near-term catalyst for re-rating. Q3 FY2026 (Feb 2026) showed EPS of $0.35, down 35% YoY from $0.54, with revenue essentially flat at $11.28B. Operating income collapsed to $650M from $844M YoY, and operating cash flow plunged 76% to $430M. The company faces eight consecutive quarters of Greater China declines (down 12% last quarter), loss of market share in running shoes to On and Hoka, and a $1.5B annual tariff headwind. Net margin has compressed from 9.4% to 4.8% over the past year, while ROE has fallen from 32.2% to 16%. The stock trades at 27x diluted P/E on depressed earnings, which is expensive given the trajectory—earnings have declined 14.7% annually over five years. The Q4 FY2026 earnings beat was largely driven by a one-time $986M tariff refund, masking underlying weakness. News sentiment is negative (mean -0.146), and the stock has fallen 75% from its peak with no clear catalyst for recovery. Management's cautious guidance and reduced disclosures (pulling back on gender breakdowns) signal ongoing operational challenges rather than a turnaround.
